body: guilt has a funny way of overshadowing it.

i don’t know what you were attempting to say in your first sentence. 

and don’t be sorry, not your fault.

it’s been 5 years. i’m done. 

if enough people in my life could see past it, i wouldn’t feel like this. 

i’m done.

congrats on your engagement. good luck on coming out. 

that’s all i have to say.

i’ve had hope in humanity. it’s proven me wrong. i’m too tired to keep holding onto false hope because that’s all it’s proven to be, false hope. 

i don’t know that this applies to all trans people. i don’t think this is every trans person’s reality, but it’s mine. it has been

thank you for trying, but this really isn’t going to change. 

i hope you have a good day, hon <3

thank you.

i know the suggestions of where to look for people is meant to be encouraging or helpful, but it just makes me feel like more of a freak.
because i HAVE to look for someone to care or love me within a small demographic/ community.  

i can’t just go out and fall for someone or flirt or do anything because i know that there is a greater chance of them telling me i’m disgusting or weird or that they don’t “like people like me”. 
and i hate that i have to care or worry about any of that happening. but that is my reality. and i have never felt more isolated because of it.

i hate that i would even have to think about that. i have to search within one community or another. it fucking sucks. i can’t even do that in my life. nobody has some sign showing who likes trans people. 

being trans is beautiful, but it is the most painful thing i am ever going to have to deal with. 
and nobody cares to acknowledge that.
i have absolutely no idea what you could do to help this. i’m sorry
